batch_strategy: Freeze these 32 IDs and their supplied packet predictions before any label reveal. Combine matched loading and solvent-response experiments in recently exposed failure regions with focused structural-transfer tests in unmeasured ester, ketone, aldehyde, and oxygen-heterocycle families. Prioritize relationships that can generalize across catalog rows; use CW distance and quantile spans as supporting signals, without interpreting them as calibrated epistemic uncertainty.

choices.reason: m72 at 5/1, 153.3 mg, and 200 uL DCM starts a three-ratio curve at threefold the loading of measured 10f01f359bc6067d009f. Together with the selected 10/1 and 20/1 rows, it tests whether the unusual low-loading response transfers across loading.

m72 at 10/1 and 153.3 mg directly contrasts with 7383949c431e18f39597 at 51.1 mg, whose acquisition V2 prediction exceeded measurement by 50.95 mL. Current predictions nearly ignore this loading change; the label tests whether the corrected 10/1 response generalizes.

m72 at 20/1 and 153.3 mg completes the matched high-loading curve and contrasts with 1b1a9ec85268aa66d327 at 51.1 mg. Its predicted 34.63/107.91 mL endpoints test whether the large 10/1-to-20/1 increase persists across loading or is specific to the existing observations.

m125 at 1/1, 150 mg, and 500 uL DCM matches measured 03744855d469f4cca7e6 at 300 uL. This tests whether the large completion-volume difference at 100 mg in 4c32851430464f0ed684 and dbb94bf062fc0e640258 persists at higher loading.

m125 at 5/1, 50 mg, and 300 uL DCM matches measured 761c3f82d640da44966c at 500 uL. With the measured 150 mg pair 549daca56bed1c9d2bcc and 06ebbf6e52fa3ea6aef3, it completes a loading-by-injection-volume rectangle where onset and completion may respond differently.

m141 at 10/1 and 92 mg lies between measured 46 and 138 mg rows 7fb4f90753d40dd25be0 and 6f548d72f01fc85debdc. Those rows differ by 13.31 mL in onset but only 0.79 mL in completion; this point tests the loading-response shape that nearly invariant predictions cannot describe.

m94 at 10/1 and 58.7 mg directly contrasts with 5b445b457a8b897a2d6c at 176.1 mg. The measured 20/1 pair ffc70e28db22d1cc1f3f and ffffcd6f3b9393846ab4 showed a substantial onset difference with similar completion, so this label tests whether that association also occurs at an intermediate ratio.

m204 at 5/1 and 150.15 mg fills the matched gap between 6a39aff909ea35989c74 at 2/1 and 73502a52708e4f9c2391 at 10/1. The latter measured 51.71/94.93 mL after substantial underprediction; this label identifies curvature instead of adding another endpoint correction.

m60 at 5/1 and 97 mg fills the same response interval selected for primary alcohol m204, using measured 4b3e648044ebe5372a27 and c352863d9fa4a8645481 as its own anchors. It tests whether secondary and primary OH environments differ in where retention begins to rise sharply.

m167 at 10/1 and 150 mg matches its measured 50/1 row fa6fd34875fdc7acf6c1 and the m166 10/1 row 20acd2ae49790ab82053. The predicted completion of 22.17 mL is already close to m167's measured 50/1 completion of 22.40 mL, testing a shallow curve and the effect of aromatic extension.

m75 at 10/1 and 54.75 mg extends the exact-loading series containing 3726956d81fe3954e5b7 at 20/1 and 28e9fea3e3293f2b8a0e at 50/1. Their completion volumes decrease from 30.51 to 11.63 mL; this interior label tests whether the recorded curve is already irregular before that reversal.

m75 at 20/1 and 164.25 mg provides a threefold loading contrast to 3726956d81fe3954e5b7 under the same injection conditions. It tests whether the retained 20/1 observation transfers across loading, helping prevent the surprising 50/1 result from becoming an unjustified scaffold-wide correction.

Methyl thioglycolate m96 at 10/1 and 59.35 mg extends measured 6dde3c4535c931ca4092 at 5/1, which gave 9.59/12.50 mL. The predicted 14.45/25.48 mL endpoints test an unmeasured increase for a thiol-containing ester, a less-covered interaction environment than the oxygen-only ester families.

m96 at 20/1 matches the selected 10/1 loading and injection conditions. Its predicted 24.12/55.72 mL endpoints imply a further steep increase; high CW distance supports measuring this response directly rather than transferring an oxygen-donor or ester slope to sulfur chemistry.

Unsaturated aliphatic aldehyde m53 at 10/1 and 133.2 mg anchors the selected weak-eluent contrast. Measured 59bbda2fab97a5d45827 establishes early elution at 2/1 and lower loading, but does not establish the predicted weak-eluent curve at this loading.

m53 at 50/1 matches the selected 10/1 conditions, with predictions rising from 6.50/13.70 to 23.63/50.28 mL. This high-CW-distance pair tests whether a flexible, hydrophobic aldehyde follows a steep response despite modest retention at stronger eluent.

Methyl acetoacetate m95 at 50/1 and 161.4 mg matches the loading of measured 35944fdd59ac331c3fcb at 10/1. The predicted 26.20/63.39 mL endpoints test weak-eluent transfer within beta-ketoesters after m94 and m82 exposed substantial underprediction, while aromatic beta-diketones behaved differently.

tert-Butyl acetoacetate m25 at 50/1 and 95.4 mg tests how ester substitution changes the beta-ketoester response. Measured 327064e6ca2c38d79d76 provides a retained 20/1 anchor at lower loading; the new label complements selected m95 without assuming that this cross-molecule comparison isolates a single causal effect.

Unmeasured branched-chain acrylate m16 at 5/1 and 44.25 mg anchors a focused ester transfer test. Related long-chain acrylate m18 is early-eluting in measured dbe79bb4ca4ae4967721 at 5/1, whereas m16 is predicted to become much more retained at weak eluent.

m16 at 50/1 matches the selected 5/1 conditions and is predicted at 20.12/41.22 mL. The strong predicted response of this H-bond-donor-free acrylate tests whether chain environment and ester accessibility are represented correctly, rather than inferring retention from hydrophobicity alone.

Unmeasured bromobenzodioxole m6 at 5/1 and 83.45 mg anchors a two-oxygen ring environment with only moderate similarity to observed molecules. Measured bromobenzofuran m8 row 898bde0c214429571108 supplies a related, but not condition-matched, heterocycle reference.

m6 at 50/1 matches the selected 5/1 conditions, testing a predicted rise from 6.19/10.89 to 10.78/22.81 mL. This pair adds an interpretable solvent slope for a new oxygen heterocycle rather than a single molecular offset.

Unmeasured deoxybenzoin m171 at 5/1 and 120 mg anchors a ketone containing one benzyl and one directly conjugated phenyl group. Its predicted 7.34/15.20 mL endpoints allow the selected 20/1 label to distinguish a molecular offset from an unusual solvent response.

m171 at 20/1 matches the selected 5/1 conditions but has lower predicted endpoints, 6.25/13.04 mL. This untested reversal is a useful transfer check after measured carbonyl compounds showed both steep responses and early-eluting exceptions.

Unmeasured chlorobenzophenone m176 at 5/1 and 100 mg anchors a diaryl-ketone comparison with methoxybenzophenone m114 and dimethylbenzophenone m131. Those observed families have markedly different weak-eluent behavior, so substitution effects merit a local curve rather than a functional-group average.

m176 at 50/1 matches the selected 5/1 conditions and is predicted at 11.59/33.76 mL. Measured 44fcf641ccfa3b10a97c for m114 and c060c367e4e5bf6955cb for m131 gave completion volumes of 75.88 and 26.05 mL at 50/1 and 100 mg; this label tests transfer to chlorine substitution, acknowledging different injection volumes.

Unmeasured ortho-tolualdehyde m145 at 5/1 and 103.9 mg anchors a positional-substitution comparison with meta-tolualdehyde m142 and dimethyl aldehyde m134. The latter has a measured 5/1 anchor in 5fe9702f3a3a783b4c94, providing nearby chemistry without establishing the ortho effect.

m145 at 50/1 matches the selected 5/1 conditions and tests the predicted 10.94/24.05 mL endpoints. Its moderate predicted response supplies a useful contrast to steeper carbonyl curves and tests whether local substitution effects generalize to an unseen positional isomer.

Unmeasured isoamyl benzoate m55 at 10/1 and 99 mg anchors transfer from isobutyl benzoate m56. Measured 19e665b6098744dfb60c establishes early elution for m56 at 10/1 and lower loading; the selected pair tests whether the additional methylene changes the response across eluent strength.

m55 at 40/1 matches the selected 10/1 conditions, with predictions increasing from 6.14/10.75 to 9.93/20.65 mL. This moderate-retention ester pair expands coverage of the densely represented benzoate family without concentrating all labels in extreme-retention regions.

Unmeasured biphenyl aldehyde m189 at 2/1 and 110.7 mg anchors an aromatic-topology comparison with naphthaldehyde m195. Measured 1194ed3b17f8c39d6111 gives a stronger-eluent m195 reference; fused and linked aromatic systems need not share a retention slope.

m189 at 20/1 matches the selected 2/1 conditions and tests its predicted 11.68/23.44 mL endpoints. The m195 20/1 observations 783cf2454912fc14bb80 and a917c928912c74862968 differ substantially, so a new related curve can improve structural transfer without treating either observation as a universal aromatic-extension rule.

hypotheses.content: For m141 and m94, lower recorded loading is associated with later onset at the measured ratios, while completion changes much less. The magnitude and ratio dependence remain unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Nearly loading-invariant predictions can miss endpoint-specific condition effects. These contrasts can teach the model to change V1 without imposing the same change on V2.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m141's intermediate loading interpolate its onset difference, and does m94 show the same loading association at 10/1 as at 20/1?

hypotheses.content: The recorded m72 response has a large increase between 10/1 and 20/1, while its measured 5/1-to-10/1 change is small and negative. Whether this shape persists across loading is unresolved; the small reversal could reflect observational variability.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The latest 10/1 label exposed a 50.95 mL acquisition-time V2 overprediction. A second complete loading curve tests whether retraining learned a transferable transition or simply fitted the original rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 153.3 mg with 200 uL DCM, do the 5/1, 10/1, and 20/1 labels reproduce the low-loading shape?

hypotheses.content: m125's association with DCM injection volume depends on ratio and endpoint. Larger injection volume increased measured completion in pure EA, at 1/1, and at 2/1, but the 150 mg pair at 5/1 had similar completion and substantially different onset.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The model still gives almost identical predictions across injection volumes. Completing matched contrasts can distinguish a ratio-dependent association from a molecular offset, while unrecorded variables limit causal attribution.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the 1/1 completion difference persist at 150 mg, and does the 5/1 onset difference persist at 50 mg?

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl response transfer depends strongly on structural environment. The steep beta-ketoester curves do not transfer uniformly to aromatic beta-diketones or other ketones. The m75 weak-eluent reversal is an unresolved recorded exception, not an established mechanistic rule.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Recent errors have opposite signs across carbonyl families. Local analogue curves can teach structure-by-eluent interactions and reduce inappropriate sharing of slopes based only on carbonyl counts.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the m167, m95, m25, m171, and m176 labels support their distinct predicted curves, and is m75's retained 20/1 behavior robust to loading?

hypotheses.content: Both primary alcohol m204 and secondary alcohol m60 have steep measured 2/1-to-10/1 responses, with a larger increase for m204 under its recorded conditions. Their intermediate curvature remains unmeasured.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The latest labels supported the steep-response hypothesis but exceeded predicted retention, especially for m204. Interior points can separate response curvature from endpoint offsets and improve transfer among alcohol environments.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed conditions within each molecule, where do the 5/1 labels fall between the measured 2/1 and 10/1 endpoints?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes strengthen the steep-response hypotheses for m204 and m60, but show that their intermediate slopes still need measurement. Lutidine and m94 now provide a more specific loading pattern: onset differs substantially across loading while completion is comparatively stable. This shifts follow-up toward endpoint-specific condition learning. m125's pure-EA result preserves a completion-volume difference between injection volumes, whereas its 5/1 pair has nearly equal completion and reversed onset ordering relative to the 1/1 pair; a universal injection-volume offset is inadequate. m202's 183.45 mg result of 4.62/9.38 mL rejects a simple monotonic loading explanation of its 10/1 series. I retain that inconsistency as unresolved rather than extrapolating a loading rule. The m72 10/1 label rejects the previously predicted large intermediate completion volume and motivates a second loading curve. The m166 and m167 outcomes weaken the predicted steep aromatic beta-diketone response, while m75's 50/1 result introduces an unexpected reversal needing cautious follow-up. Oxime m11 at 50/1 measured 43.11/119.20 mL, supporting a late steep response and weakening the earlier concern that its weak-eluent growth was excessive. m27's new labels support its early-eluting exception and indicate successful local repair, so it receives no further labels here. The recent ketone analogue results were generally less severe than the alcohol, m72, and dicarbonyl failures; their value now lies more in structural transfer than repeated repair. Historical errors are acquisition-time errors, not current residuals. I also correct a memory citation: observed 8b59c86480a0a3337c63 is m57, while the m179 20/1 observation is 8b8becd233748ccae9e3.
batch_rationale: The batch links recent failures to experiments that distinguish response shape, structural transfer, and recorded condition effects. The m72 three-ratio curve tests a large transition at a second loading. The m125 contrasts complete useful portions of an injection-volume/loading design, while m141 and m94 test onset-specific loading associations. Intermediate alcohol labels constrain recently underpredicted curves. Carbonyl selections connect shallow aromatic beta-diketone behavior, steep beta-ketoesters, a surprising malonate reversal, and unseen ketone environments. New acrylate, benzoate, aldehyde, and oxygen-heterocycle pairs provide both molecular anchors and solvent slopes, including moderate-retention cases relevant to the broad Row-distribution. The m96 and m53 pairs test large predicted weak-eluent changes in less-covered functional environments. Multiple rows per molecule are retained when they identify a relationship; no identical-condition duplicate rows are selected. Comparisons across molecules are interpreted with their different loadings and injection volumes in view. The batch is intended to improve generalization after retraining by separating molecular offsets from condition-dependent responses, with observational variability and missing experimental variables remaining limits on mechanistic interpretation and expected benefit.
